scope_justification: A human-made signal processing construct: a quantifiable property extracted from the time-domain representation of an audio signal that captures a specific characteristic useful for analysis, classification, or retrieval.

Sociolinguistics is a human-made discipline — the scientific study of how language varies across and within social groups — built to persist as a stable field of analysis in dialectology, variationist fieldwork, and language policy.

Voice range profile is a human-made clinical graph mapping the range of fundamental frequencies a voice can produce at each loudness level, devised to quantify a speaker's phonatory range in voice-disorder assessment.

The root-mean-square amplitude of a power spectrum across a frequency range. Computed as the square root of the mean of squared spectral amplitude values, providing a measure of the effective signal strength in a spectrum.
SPECTRAL ANALYSIS PARAMETER

A human-made laryngeal parameter that quantifies the air pressure in the subglottal space during phonation, built to persist as a standardized clinical measure of laryngeal effort and hyperfunctional phonation in laryngology and speech-language pathology.
A contiguous frequency range within the overall spectrum, used for partitioning spectral analysis into independent bands for subband coding, filter bank design, and band-specific feature extraction.
The Shannon entropy of the normalized energy distribution across frequency bins within a defined frequency band [f_low, f_high], measuring the uniformity or concentration of spectral energy.

Voice specialists and researchers made it to quantify how voice disorders affect a patient's daily life, social functioning, and emotional well-being — shifting assessment from clinician-centered measures to the patient's own reported experience.

Intonation is the human-constructed linguistic dimension of pitch organization in speech: the systematic, rule-governed framework by which utterances use rising and falling pitch to carry grammar, focus, and attitude — built to be transcribed, taught, and analyzed across generations of speakers and linguists.

A human-made mathematical construct in signal processing: a complex-valued representation formed by adding the original real signal as its real part and the Hilbert transform of that signal as its imaginary part, enabling direct extraction of instantaneous amplitude, phase, and frequency.
A human-made analytical construct measuring the difference between the current spectral energy and the maximum spectral energy, used in audio analysis

A human-made voice-quality measurement parameter quantifying the asymmetry of the glottal airflow pulse in voiced phonation, built to persist as a standardized clinical parameter in speech science and laryngology.

Researchers made the glottal-area-waveform construct to represent the time-varying cross-sectional area of the glottis during phonation, so that clinicians and voice scientists can quantify cycle-by-cycle glottal dynamics beyond steady-state descriptions.

A human-made linguistic concept: the systematic variation of pitch (fundamental frequency) across utterances to encode grammatical structure (e.g., question vs statement), pragmatic attitude (e.g., sarcasm, emphasis), and discourse organization. Built to persist as a descriptive construct in linguistic analysis.
A human-made audio processing metric: the root-mean-square energy of a signal over a temporal window. Fundamental for speech processing, onset detection, and loudness estimation.

A human-made voice-quality measurement parameter quantifying the fraction of the fundamental period during which the glottis is open, estimated from the glottal-flow waveform, built to persist as a standardized clinical parameter in speech science and laryngology.

Historical linguistics is a human-made discipline — the scientific study of how languages change over time and of the genealogical relations among related languages — built to persist as a stable field of analysis in the comparative tradition, in historical grammars, and in the classification of the world's languages.

A human-made mathematical transform used in signal processing to separate periodic structures in a spectrum by transforming the log-power spectrum into a quefrency domain, revealing repeating spectral patterns as distinct peaks. Built to persist as an intermediate representation in speech analysis, audio processing, and structural detection.
A human-made family of standardized clinical parameters for assessing vocal health, built to persist as the maintained measurement map of voice-disorder assessment in laryngology and speech science.

A normalized measure of how much of a band's total energy resides in a single frequency bin, expressed as the ratio of that bin's energy to the sum of all bin energies within the band — enabling cross-band comparison independent of absolute energy level.
A spectral feature that quantifies the effective width of the energy distribution within a frequency band, computed from the second-order statistics of the energy distribution.
THING

People made the vocal fold construct to map and categorize the paired mucosal structures within the larynx that vibrate to produce phonation, so that clinicians can identify their normal anatomy, pathological changes, and surgical landmarks.
A human-made analytical construct representing the phase component of the short-time Fourier transform spectrum, used in audio synthesis and phase-vocoder applications

A human-made spectral analysis measure quantifying how concentrated or peaked the per-bin energy distribution is within a defined frequency sub-band, used in instrument recognition and voice activity detection.

A human-made spectral analysis construct that divides the frequency spectrum into contiguous octave-band subbands, each covering a frequency range where the upper bound is twice the lower bound, used in acoustics and psychoacoustic analysis

The ordered per-bin energy vector of a full spectrum — the complete N-tuple of non-negative bin energies covering all frequency bins, unbounded by any sub-band, which serves as the substrate operand for full-spectrum spectral descriptors.

People made the vocal fold vibration construct to model and classify the self-sustained oscillatory motion of the vocal folds during phonation, so that clinicians and researchers can characterize normal versus pathological voice production.
A signal processing construct measuring the duration from the onset of a sound to the peak of its amplitude envelope

A human-made voice-quality measurement parameter quantifying the steepest negative slope of the glottal airflow pulse within the glottal cycle (the maximum flow declination), built to persist as a standardized clinical parameter of the glottal source parameter set in speech science and laryngology.

A family of spectral analysis parameters that operate within a defined frequency sub-band rather than over the full spectrum. Each parameter reduces the per-bin energy vector of a band to a scalar summary statistic — capturing distribution shape, energy concentration, temporal change, or moment-based properties localized to analyst-specified frequency bounds.

A human-made voice-quality parameter locating the point of glottal closure within each glottal cycle of voiced phonation, estimated from the glottal flow waveform, built to persist as a standardized clinical measure in speech science and laryngology.

A hand-computed descriptor of audio spectra that quantifies the tailedness of a power spectrum around its spectral centroid. Built to persist as a scalar value stored per spectral frame for use in classification, anomaly detection, and timbre analysis pipelines.

A human-made voice-quality measurement parameter that quantifies the duration or area of a specified phase within the glottal cycle as a proportion of the fundamental period, built to persist as a generalized framework for quantifying temporal and geometric relationships in glottal phonation in speech science and laryngology.

Accent is the human-constructed sociolinguistic dimension of the phonological component of a speech variety: the distinctive sound patterns by which listeners identify a speaker's regional or social origin — built to be indexed in speech communities, dialect atlases, and sociolinguistic analysis across generations.

A human-made physiological construct of the vocal-fold vibration process during voiced phonation, built to persist as the foundational phenomenon underlying glottal airflow and vocal-fold contact in speech science and clinical laryngology.

A human-made spectral representation of the glottal source: the per-frame power spectrum of the glottal flow waveform (glottogram), built to persist as a standardized diagnostic representation in speech science and laryngology.

Corpus-linguistics is a human-made approach to linguistics — the study of language based on large, systematically collected bodies of real-language data (corpora), built to persist as a stable empirical method in empirical linguistics, language technology, and lexicography.

A human-made voice-quality measurement parameter quantifying the temporal offset between glottal-source onset and acoustic voice onset in the first phonation cycle, built to persist as a standardized clinical parameter in speech science and laryngology that classifies breathy, modal, and creaky phonation.
Spectral-band-moment is a human-authored map of spectral analysis parameters: band-localized moments of spectral energy distribution, with made boundaries defining the moment order and band limits.

A human-made voice-quality measurement category quantifying cycle-to-cycle variations in the amplitude (energy) of voiced speech, built to persist as a standardized measurement class in speech science and laryngology for voice-disorder assessment.
A human-made mathematical model of speech production, built to persist as a theoretical framework in speech science and computational phonetics.

A standardized clinical index built to quantify glottal efficiency during phonation by relating subglottal pressure to phonatory flow, built to persist as a measure of vocal effort and voice-disorder severity.

A human-authored temporal analysis construct that describes the evolution, transport, and redistribution of spectral energy patterns across time, used in music information retrieval and audio scene analysis
A human-made full-spectrum energy-quantile summary reporting the median frequency of a signal's spectral energy distribution.
SPECTRAL ANALYSIS PARAMETER

A human-made linguistic concept: the relative prominence assigned to one syllable over others within a word or phrase, realized through combinations of pitch, duration, and intensity. Built to persist as an analytical construct for describing syllable-level prominence patterns across languages.
The vector of energy values across individual frequency bins within a defined frequency band, serving as the foundational data object for all spectral-band feature computations.

Researchers made high-speed videolaryngoscopy to record vocal fold vibration at true temporal resolution — capturing rapid subglottal events, collision dynamics, and asymmetries that stroboscopy aliases or blurs — so they can study vibratory mechanics that require real-time recording.

Text-linguistics is a human-made discipline of linguistics — the study of the structure, coherence, and function of extended texts (discourses) as structured wholes, built to persist as a stable field of analysis in discourse studies, rhetoric, and text technology.

Cognitive-linguistics is a human-made approach to linguistics — the study of language as shaped by general cognitive abilities including categorization, conceptualization, and embodied experience, built to persist as a stable theoretical framework in theoretical linguistics, cognitive science, and language acquisition research.

Speaking fundamental frequency is a human-made acoustic parameter — the average fundamental frequency of the voice signal during connected speech — devised to characterize a speaker's voice in speech analysis.
Voice break is a human-made clinical event — the abrupt interruption or discontinuity in the voice signal during phonation — devised to describe a sign observed in voice-disorder assessment.

A human-made construct of the acoustic waveform produced by the speech production apparatus, built to persist as the primary analysis signal in speech science — the physical medium from which voice quality, prosody, and articulatory parameters are extracted through signal processing.

A human-made voice-quality parameter quantifying the peak glottal flow within each glottal cycle, built to persist as a standardized clinical measure of glottal source dynamics and voice-disorder assessment in laryngology and speech-language pathology.

A sociolect is a variety of language associated with a particular social group or social class, distinguished by systematic conventions in lexicon, pronunciation, and grammar. Human-made as a sociolinguistic category — the map of how social identity shapes linguistic practice.

A human-made spectral analysis measure quantifying the median energy location across the full spectrum at a given analysis frame — the frequency at which cumulative energy reaches 50 percent of the total — standardized for use in music information retrieval and audio classification.
A human-made analytical construct measuring the ratio of peak spectral magnitude to mean spectral magnitude, used as an indicator of impulse-to-average energy ratio in audio signals

Clinicians made stroboscopy to visualize vocal fold mucosal wave and vibratory symmetry — information invisible at real-time observation — so they can detect subtle mucosal pathology that affects voice quality.

A human-made audio engineering metric: the ratio of peak amplitude to RMS amplitude of a signal. Used to characterize the dynamic profile of audio signals, distinguish percussive from sustained sounds, and guide compression strategies.

A spectral analysis measure quantifying how much of a full spectrum's total energy resides in a single frequency bin, expressed as the ratio of that bin's energy to the sum of all bin energies, enabling cross-spectrum comparison independent of absolute energy level.

A human-made glottal-geometry measurement construct quantifying the time-varying cross-sectional area of the glottal aperture across the glottal cycle, built to persist as the geometric base waveform of the area-quotient family (open, closed, contact, and area-moment quotients) in speech science and laryngology.

A human-made voice-quality parameter quantifying the absolute average of consecutive fundamental-period differences in voiced speech, built to persist as a standardized clinical measure of period instability in voice-disorder assessment.

Otolaryngologists and speech-language pathologists created this classification to categorize bilateral benign growths on the vocal fold free edge — the most common cause of chronic hoarseness in children and young adults — enabling standardized diagnosis and treatment planning across laryngology practice.
A time-frequency representation where the frequency axis is warped according to the bark scale — a psychoacoustic frequency scale approximating human ear critical-band resolution.

A human-made measurement construct of the periodic airflow excitation pulse generated by vocal fold vibration during voiced phonation, built to persist as the source phenomenon underlying glottal airflow and vocal-fold contact in speech science and clinical laryngology.
To standardize the measurement of period ratio instability in voiced speech for diagnosing voice disorders in clinical laryngology and speech science.

A human-made measurement construct quantifying the cycle-to-cycle variation of a periodic parameter in voiced speech — the deviation from regularity that distinguishes stable phonation from dysphonic or irregular phonation — built to persist as a standardized classification of voice instability in speech science and laryngology.
A standardized acoustic parameter representing the third formant frequency, built to persist as a diagnostic measure of vocal-tract shape and resonance characteristics in voice-disorder assessment.

A human-made mathematical construct — a parameterized family of window functions defined by the zeroth-order modified Bessel function, designed to achieve optimal tradeoff between main-lobe width and side-lobe attenuation for spectral analysis.
To standardize the measurement of period instability in voiced speech for diagnosing voice disorders in clinical laryngology and speech science.
SPECTRAL ANALYSIS PARAMETER
A human-made clinical diagnostic category grouping voice disorders, built so laryngology and speech-language pathology can refer, code, and treat disordered phonation under one shared unit.
SIGNAL PROCESSING METRIC

A human-made spectral analysis measure quantifying how evenly energy is distributed across bins within a defined frequency sub-band, normalized to a 0–1 scale for use in timbre comparison and instrument classification.

A normalized measure of spectral energy dispersion within a frequency sub-band, expressed as the coefficient of variation of per-bin energies — the ratio of the standard deviation to the mean energy — enabling cross-band comparison independent of absolute energy level.
A ratio metric comparing spectral peak energy to average energy within a frequency band
test

A human-made classification category made by laryngology and speech science to name the normal periodic mode of phonation so that breathy and creaky voice can be classified as deviations from it in clinical assessment and voice training.

A human-made voice-quality measurement of phonation: the proportion of the glottal cycle during which the vocal folds remain in contact, built to persist as a per-frame measure of vocal-fold contact in speech science and clinical laryngology.

A human-made spectral analysis parameter measuring the asymmetry of energy distribution within a frequency sub-band — how unevenly energy is distributed across the band's bins, complementing the centroid (center), spread (width), and skewness (direction) descriptors.

A human-made psychoacoustic construct representing the frequency resolution unit of the human auditory system — the effective bandwidth of auditory filters at a given center frequency. It quantifies how the ear separates frequencies into perceptually independent channels, used in sound design, audio analysis, and psychoacoustic modeling.

Computational linguistics is a human-made discipline — the systematic application of computational methods to the analysis and processing of natural language — built to persist as a stable field in language software, annotated corpora, and shared computational representations of linguistic structure.

A human-made voice-quality measurement parameter quantifying the cycle-to-cycle variation of the fundamental period in a voiced speech signal, built to persist as a standardized clinical parameter in speech science and laryngology.

A human-made classification category made by laryngology and speech science to name the two-pitched double-voice mode of phonation so it can be told apart from the other phonation modes in clinical assessment and voice training.

A human-authored temporal tracking construct that follows the evolution of spectral centroid position across consecutive analysis frames, used in music information retrieval for tracking timbral motion and audio scene analysis
Formant frequency is a human-made acoustic parameter — a resonance frequency of the vocal tract appearing as an energy concentration in the speech spectrum — devised to characterize speech sounds.

People made the larynx construct to map and categorize the human neck organ that houses the vocal folds and mediates breathing, phonation, and airway protection, so that clinicians and anatomists can consistently locate, describe, and treat pathologies in this region.

A standardized acoustic power measure built to quantify loudness level and vocal effort in clinical voice assessment and signal-processing practice.

A human-made voice-quality measurement parameter quantifying the fraction of the fundamental period during which the vocal folds are in contact, estimated from the electroglottographic signal, built to persist as a standardized clinical parameter in speech science and laryngology.
A human-made analytical construct that identifies the frequency below which a specified percentage of total spectral energy is concentrated, used for timbral characterization

A human-authored ordering construct that arranges cepstral coefficients into a indexed sequence for spectral analysis, enabling pattern recognition and feature extraction in speech and audio processing

A human-made voice-quality measurement parameter quantifying the relative average of second-order period differences between consecutive glottal cycles in voiced speech, built to persist as a standardized clinical parameter for period instability assessment in laryngology and speech science.

A human-made per-frame time-series representation of estimated glottal airflow derived from inverse filtering of the speech signal, used as the foundational waveform for voice-quality parameter computation and source-filter analysis.

Accent is the sociolinguistic category isolating the phonological component of a speech variety as an independently indexable unit of origin identification — built to persist through dialect atlases, sociolinguistic pedagogy, and the accent-labeling conventions of scholarship and media.

A hand-computed descriptor of audio spectra that quantifies the asymmetry of a power spectrum around its spectral centroid. Built to persist as a scalar value stored per spectral frame for use in classification and analysis pipelines.

A human-made linear filter whose impulse response is an exponentially-modulated sinusoid (a gamma-shaped envelope), realized as a cascade of resonator sections to model the frequency selectivity of the auditory periphery; the dynamic counterpart to the static triangular mel-filter-bank.
A human-authored distance-measurement framework that quantifies dissimilarity or similarity between spectral shapes, enabling classification, clustering, and retrieval in audio and speech analysis

A human-made spectral feature that quantifies the fraction of frequency bins in a power spectrum that exceed a noise-floor threshold, indicating the active bandwidth or tonal density of a signal frame. Built for speech activity detection, music source separation, and acoustic scene analysis where knowing how many frequency bands are active matters more than their exact values.

The ordered tuple of non-negative per-bin energy values from a spectral decomposition, indexed by bin center frequency over a contiguous bin range — the shared substrate operand of full-spectrum and band-restricted spectral descriptors.

A human-made classification category made by laryngology and speech science to name the low-frequency implosive vibration mode of phonation so it can be told apart from modal phonation in clinical assessment and voice training.
People made it to see the larynx on a monitor, to record, transmit, and guide the airway without the mirror's line-of-sight limit.

A human-made measurement construct of the duration of the closed (adducted/contact) phase of the glottal cycle during voiced phonation, built to persist as a per-cycle time parameter in speech science and clinical voice assessment.

A human-made voice-quality parameter quantifying the balance between the periodic (harmonic) and the aperiodic (noise-like) components of the glottal source spectrum, built to persist as a standardized clinical parameter of the glottal source parameter set in speech science and laryngology.

A scalar width descriptor of a signal's spectral energy distribution: the width of the ideal rectangular pulse having the same peak height and the same total energy as the distribution (the peak-normalized effective bandwidth), distinct from the centroid-spread bandwidth.

A human-made spectral feature quantifying the ratio between the energy of spectral peaks and valleys within a frequency range, used to characterize the peakedness and tonal structure of audio signals.

People made the glottis construct to map and categorize the opening between the vocal folds within the larynx, so that clinicians can assess airway patency, phonation efficiency, and pathology at this critical constriction point.

A human-made signal processing technique that inverts a system's transfer function to recover the original excitation signal — the residual after removing the estimated filtering effect. Persisted through textbook treatment in DSP (Rabiner and Schafer), implementation in speech analysis toolkits (Praat, MATLAB, Kaldi), and standard use in source-filter separation.
An algorithmic construct for inferring the beat rate of a periodic audio signal as a quantitative measure in beats per minute

Psycholinguistics is a human-made discipline — the scientific study of the cognitive and neural mechanisms by which languages are acquired, produced, and understood — built to persist as a stable field of analysis in experimental psychology, developmental science, and the neurosciences.

A human-made laryngeal voice-quality parameter that quantifies the minimum subglottal pressure required to initiate vocal-fold vibration, built to persist as a standardized clinical and experimental measure of vocal-fold load and laryngeal biomechanics in laryngology and speech science.

A psychoacoustic construct describing the frequency resolution limits of the auditory system: a bandpass region within which the ear integrates acoustic energy as a single unit. Human-made because it is a mathematical map (Bark scale, ERB function) imposed on natural hearing to quantify spectral integration zones.

A human-made physiological construct of vocal-fold apposition during the glottal cycle, built to persist as the physical phenomenon underlying glottal airflow and vocal-fold contact in speech science and clinical laryngology.

A human-made physiological construct of vocal-fold contact area during the glottal cycle, built to persist as the physical measure underlying electroglottography and glottal contact in speech science and clinical laryngology.

A human-made voice-quality parameter quantifying the ratio of harmonic (voiced) energy to noise energy in a speech signal, built to persist as a standardized clinical measure of phonation type and voice-disorder assessment in laryngology and speech-language pathology.

A human-made spectral analysis measure quantifying the ratio of the strongest to the average spectral energy across the full spectrum at a given analysis frame, standardized for use in music information retrieval and audio classification.
SPECTRAL ANALYSIS PARAMETER
A spectral feature that measures the root-mean-square (RMS) energy within a frequency band, providing a magnitude measure that accounts for the energy of all bins rather than just the peak.
A human-made model of the glottal airflow source in speech production theory, built to persist as the source component in the source-filter model.

A human-made signal processing construct — the residual waveform obtained by removing a known or estimated system transfer function from an observed signal, yielding the estimated input that drove the system. In speech analysis, the excitation signal is the glottal-flow waveform estimated by inverting the vocal-tract transfer function; in general DSP, it is the recovered source signal after inverse filtering of any linear system.

People made the mucosal wave construct to model and classify the traveling wave motion of the vocal fold surface during phonation, so that clinicians can assess tissue health and detect pathology via visual or acoustic inspection.
SPECTRAL ANALYSIS PARAMETER
A human-made two-dimensional data structure that arranges spectral magnitude or power values across both time and frequency dimensions, used for visual and computational analysis

A spectral analysis measure quantifying the continuity of per-bin energy values across a full spectrum, computed as a normalized mean absolute derivative of adjacent bin energies, enabling comparison of spectral smoothness independent of absolute energy level or number of bins.

A human-made voice-quality measurement category quantifying cycle-to-cycle variations in the fundamental period (vocal fold vibration timing) of voiced speech, built to persist as a standardized measurement class in speech science and laryngology for voice-disorder assessment.
THING

Speech-language pathologists made CAPE-V to standardize how trained raters assess voice disorder severity using a 6-dimension perceptual scale — replacing subjective global ratings with a structured, reproducible protocol that anchors each severity level to specific exemplar recordings.
To standardize the measurement of amplitude instability in voiced speech for diagnosing voice disorders in clinical laryngology and speech science.

A human-made classification category made by laryngology and speech science to name the phonation mode of incomplete glottal closure so it can be told apart from modal phonation in clinical assessment and voice training.

Neurolinguistics is a human-made interdisciplinary field — the study of the neural and biological mechanisms underlying language acquisition, processing, and representation, built to persist as a stable field of analysis in cognitive neuroscience, speech pathology, and brain-computer interfaces for language.
A signal processing construct representing the temporal envelope of acoustic onset events in an audio signal

A human-made measurement construct of the periodic open/close cycle of the glottis during voiced phonation, comprising the opening, closed, and transition phases, built to persist as the foundational phenomenon underlying glottal airflow and vocal-fold contact in speech science and clinical laryngology.

A human-made computational model in speech science that relates glottal flow to glottal area through a first-order velocity equation, built to persist as a standard inference method for reconstructing the glottal area waveform from inverse-filtered glottal flow data.

A human-made voice-quality measurement parameter quantifying the slope of the glottal source spectrum (spectral tilt of the glottal flow waveform), built to persist as a standardized clinical parameter in speech science and laryngology.

A human-made spectral analysis parameter quantifying the ratio between the mean energy of spectral peaks and the mean energy of troughs within a defined frequency sub-band, used to characterize the peakedness and tonal structure of audio content within specific frequency ranges. Built to persist through audio coding, music information retrieval, and acoustic analysis systems.

A human-made voice-quality parameter quantifying the relative spread of consecutive fundamental periods in voiced speech, built to persist as the ratio variant of the standardized period-perturbation (jitter) measure in voice-disorder assessment.

A human-made measurement construct of the duration of the open (abducted) phase of the glottal cycle during voiced phonation, built to persist as a per-cycle time parameter in speech science and clinical voice assessment.
THING

A human-made voice-quality measurement parameter quantifying the cycle-to-cycle amplitude variation of the glottal source in voiced speech, built to persist as a standardized clinical parameter in speech science and laryngology.

A human-made voice-quality parameter quantifying the shape of the glottal area cycle by the ratio of its first to zeroth moment, built to persist as a standardized clinical index of phonatory type (creaky versus breathy voice) in voice-disorder assessment.

A human-made signal processing construct — a time-series of differences between an observed signal and its model-based reconstruction. Distinct from statistical residuals (scalar differences in regression), residual-signal is a waveform: the per-sample error between the observed signal and the output of a model system driven by the same input. In speech analysis, the residual-signal is the excitation signal obtained by inverse-filtering the speech signal through the estimated vocal-tract filter; in other domains, it is the model error waveform that reveals what the model fails to explain.

A human-made mathematical operator in signal processing that shifts the phase of every frequency component by 90 degrees, enabling construction of analytic signals and extraction of instantaneous amplitude, phase, and frequency.

The linear regression slope (in dB per Hz) of the power spectral density values across frequency bins within a defined frequency band [f_low, f_high], characterizing the spectral tilt or energy gradient.

Sound pressure level is a human-made acoustic parameter — the logarithmic measure of the sound pressure of the voice signal relative to a reference pressure — devised to quantify voice amplitude in acoustic analysis.

An utterance is the human-constructed concept for a contiguous stretch of speech or writing treated by its participants as a single unit of communicative action. Built to persist through transcription conventions, dialogue annotation systems, and the analytical frameworks of pragmatics and discourse analysis that parse continuous language use into tractable units.

A human-made voice-quality measurement parameter quantifying the return phase of the glottal airflow pulse in voiced phonation, built to persist as a standardized clinical parameter in speech science and laryngology.
A human-made spectral analysis measure quantifying how smoothly the per-bin energy values change across frequency within a defined sub-band, used in timbre characterization and audio classification.

A human-made linear bandpass filter whose center frequency and (ERB) bandwidth match the frequency selectivity of the auditory periphery at that frequency; the general construct instantiated by the gammatone-filter and approximated by the mel- and bark-filter-banks. It is the cochlear analysis filter, not the auditory filter bank that arrays them.

A human-made voice-quality measurement parameter quantifying vocal fold contact intensity as derived from the electroglottographic signal amplitude ratio, built to persist as a standardized clinical indicator of vocal fold contact strength in speech science and laryngology.
A signal processing construct that quantifies the intensity of acoustic onset events per analysis frame using spectral flux or energy-based methods

A spectral feature that quantifies the uncertainty or information content of the normalized energy distribution within a frequency band, computed using Shannon entropy over the probability mass function of per-bin energies.

People made pressed voice as a classification category to name the phonation mode of excessive glottal contact - hyperfunctional phonation - so that laryngology can tell it apart from modal and breathy phonation in voice-disorder assessment and voice therapy.

A human-made classification category made by laryngology and speech science to name the high-frequency thin-membrane mode of phonation so it can be told apart from modal phonation in clinical assessment and voice training.

A human-made mathematical construct that characterizes a spectral energy distribution through weighted frequency moments, used to summarize spectral shape in audio analysis and music information retrieval.

Voice tremor is a human-made clinical measure of the amplitude modulation of phonation — the cycle-to-cycle variation in the fundamental frequency and intensity of the voice signal — devised to quantify shaky voice in voice-disorder assessment.

A standardized signal-processing construct representing the first time derivative of the glottal flow waveform, built to provide the fundamental rate-of-change measure underlying glottal-closure dynamics parameters.

A voice-quality parameter expressing the proportion of any single phase duration (open, closed, contact) relative to the total glottal-cycle period, enabling standardized comparison of phase timing across speakers and conditions.

A human-made voice-quality measurement parameter quantifying the duration from the glottal closure instant to the time of peak glottal flow within a glottal cycle, built to persist as a standardized indicator of vocal fold closure speed and phonation type in speech science and laryngology.

A human-authored analytical construct that maps the continuity property of spectral energy distributions within frequency sub-bands. It formalizes the concept of spectral envelope smoothness for use in timbre characterization and audio classification, persisting as a computable index from FFT bin energies.

A human-made spectral analysis measure that quantifies the dispersion of energy across frequency bins within a defined sub-band, standardized for use in music information retrieval and audio classification systems.

A human-made signal processing technique that normalizes cepstral coefficient vectors by computing both the mean and variance across an utterance (or sliding window) and applying z-score normalization to each frame. Built to persist as a standard preprocessing step in speech recognition and speaker identification pipelines.

People made whisper voice as a classification category to name aperiodic airflow phonation - glottal sound without vocal-fold vibration - so that laryngology and phonetics can tell it apart from modal and creaky phonation in voice-rest care and phonetic description.

A human-made voice-quality measurement parameter quantifying the fraction of the fundamental period during which the glottis is closed, estimated from the glottal-flow waveform, built to persist as a standardized clinical parameter in speech science and laryngology.

A spectral analysis parameter representing the band-local median frequency — the frequency at which cumulative energy within a defined frequency sub-band reaches 50% of the total band energy. Distinguished from the spectral-band-centroid (mean, sensitive to outliers) by being the energy-median, providing a robust center-of-energy estimate for heavy-tailed spectral distributions.
A signal processing construct that measures per-frequency-bin absolute difference between consecutive power spectra to quantify how much spectral content has changed between adjacent frames

A human-made, frequency-dependent unit of filter bandwidth (the ERB) that describes the frequency selectivity of the auditory periphery; the bandwidth of a flat rectangular filter that would pass the same energy as a given auditory filter. The standard psychophysical unit used to set the spacing and width of gammatone, bark, and auditory-filter-bank filters.
A standardized composite clinical measure built to quantify overall voice quality by combining multiple acoustic parameters into a single scalar index for objective voice-disorder screening.

A human-made voice-quality parameter quantifying the peak rate of change of glottal flow within the glottal cycle, built to persist as a standardized clinical measure of glottal dynamics and voice-disorder assessment in laryngology and speech-language pathology.

A human-made transformation matrix used in audio signal processing that folds a frequency spectrum into 12 pitch-class bins, built to persist through its use in chroma computation across MIR toolkits and chord recognition systems.

A human-made audio analysis feature that quantifies how closely a signal's spectral content matches a periodic (harmonic) model versus a noise-like model. Built to persist through audio analysis algorithms, music information retrieval systems, and speech processing toolkits.

Stress is the human-constructed phonological dimension of prominence in speech: the systematic, rule-governed marking of certain syllables as more prominent than others — built to be transcribed, taught, and analyzed, persisting as a stable parameter of the linguistic system across generations.

A human-made spectral analysis measure quantifying how uniformly spectral energy is distributed across all frequency bins of a full spectrum at a given analysis frame — the coefficient of variation of the per-bin energies — standardized for use in music information retrieval and audio classification.

A human-made measurement construct that quantifies the fraction of the glottal cycle occupied by a specific phase of vocal fold contact or openness, computed as a ratio of time intervals within the fundamental period, built to persist as the foundational quotient family for quantifying glottal geometry in speech science and laryngology.

The system of language varieties that a speech community develops for different communicative situations — colloquial, formal, technical, ceremonial, professional — mapped along the dimensions of field, tenor, and mode. This is the LINGUISTIC sense of the word: styles of the language itself. It is distinct from the institutional sense held by the existing 'register' entry (a formal, systematically maintained official list), which is a different construct despite the shared word.

A human-made signal processing construct: the time-varying envelope of an analytic signal, extracted as its complex magnitude. Enables amplitude demodulation and envelope analysis in communication systems and audio processing.

Lexeme is a human-made conceptual map of the minimal meaningful unit that functions as the basic item in a language's mental lexicon — the abstract unit that speakers store, retrieve, and combine to produce and understand utterances. Built to persist as the fundamental atomic category of lexical semantics and morphological analysis.

A human-made signal processing construct: the time-varying frequency of a signal at each point in time, computed as the derivative of the instantaneous phase of an analytic signal. Enables real-time frequency tracking of non-stationary signals.

People made laryngology to diagnose and treat disorders of the larynx — voice disorders, airway lesions, and vocal fold pathology — by examining the folds' structure and function directly, not through the voice's acoustics alone.

A human-made signal processing construct: a bank of interrelated bandpass filters designed to decompose a signal into multiple frequency sub-bands. Built to persist as a structural component in DSP pipelines, speech analysis (mel-filterbanks), image processing, and audio effects. The bank persists through standardized implementations in software libraries (librosa, kaldi, MATLAB) and hardware DSP architectures.

A statistical measure quantifying the spread of spectral power values around their mean across frequency bins. It captures how concentrated or dispersed the spectral energy distribution is, computed from the power spectrum P[k].
A human-made audio representation: the per-frame time series of a signal's energy, obtained from a discrete-time waveform by windowing and magnitude squaring.

A spectral feature that detects and quantifies the onset of new frequency content in a signal. It measures the increase in spectral energy or the emergence of new spectral components at a given time frame, used for beat detection, transients analysis, and event segmentation.

A human-made measurement quantity of speech source analysis: the glottal airflow waveform estimated by inverse filtering of the speech signal, built to persist as the measured counterpart of the glottal-source model in speech science and clinical laryngology.

A human-made standardized perceptual voice-rating scale, built so that a trained rater's judgment of a voice sample is scored consistently across clinics and studies, persisting as the perceptual arm of voice-disorder assessment.
